topic: What antenna aperture size trade-offs exist between LEO and GEO satellites when optimizing gain and portability for CMOS-based ground terminals?
consensus_response: LEO satellites require smaller aperture sizes due to Doppler shift constraints, increasing interference and reducing network capacity. GEO satellites need larger apertures to compensate for higher orbits, introducing signal delay. Phased array antennas can mitigate these trade-offs by adaptively steering beams, balancing beamforming complexity and scanning losses.
reference_context: Satellite orbits impact antenna design, with LEO requiring complex antennas and GEO allowing fixed locations, affecting ground terminal design and network performance.
